# Contract Shape Checklist: ISK-0002 — Public Contracts & Versioning Discipline

**Purpose**: Check that the shapes of the public contract types, wire contracts, and registries are complete, unambiguous, and consistent across the spec, contract, data model, and tasks
**Created**: 2026-11-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Wire Contracts

- [x] CHK001 - Is the `error-envelope` v1 field set, field order, types, required flags, and encoding fully specified? [Completeness, Contract §`error-envelope` version 1, Research R11]
- [x] CHK002 - Is the requirement that every wire contract carry its own schema version consistent with the `resource-id` text form? [Conflict, Spec §FR-028, TR-1, Contract §`resource-id` version 1]
  - Fixed: FR-028 required every wire contract to carry its schema version in its serialized form, but the clarified ID text form (TR-1, FR-005) and the contract's grammar have no version marker. FR-028 now says the envelope carries `schema_version` in band, and the `resource-id` text has no in-band marker: its version is in the `WireContracts` registry, and any change to its text form is a break (W4). The contract says the same.
- [x] CHK003 - Is the conversion of a retry delay to the integer `after_seconds` specified? [Clarity, Contract §`error-envelope` version 1, Data model `RetryAdvice`]
  - Fixed: `RetryAfter` is a `TimeSpan` but `after_seconds` is an integer, and the rounding was unspecified. It is now whole seconds rounded up, so a client never retries before the stated time (contract, data model, T014).
- [x] CHK004 - Is the reader's behavior for unknown fields, missing required fields, wrong types, and unsupported versions specified? [Completeness, Contract §`error-envelope` version 1, Tasks T014]
- [x] CHK005 - Is it specified which retry rule requires a reset time (`limit_exceeded`) and which carries a retriable flag (`upstream_failed`)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020, Tasks T013]

## Registries

- [x] CHK006 - Does each registry have exactly one machine-readable source, and is the published contract checked against it? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Contract rule H4, Research R1]
- [x] CHK007 - Are the fields of an error code entry and a resource type entry consistent between the spec, contract, data model, and tasks? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, FR-021]
- [x] CHK008 - Do the initial resource types match the list FR-009 requires? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Contract §Resource types]
- [x] CHK009 - Are the `docs/08` reason codes registered, with their text kept recognizable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-021, Research R10]
  - Registered with the `docs/08` text as their last segment. Whether `auth_denied`'s category is right is security CHK014.
- [x] CHK010 - Are identifier rules (case, namespacing, prefix length) stated as checkable patterns? [Measurability, Data model `ErrorCode`, `ResourceType`]

## Request Context

- [x] CHK011 - Are the members of `GatewayExecutionContext` this spec owns, and the ones later specs own, clearly separated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, FR-015]
- [x] CHK012 - Is the extension mechanism for later specs specified in a way that keeps their additions compatible? [Consistency, Spec §AV-1, Research R8, Contract S7]
  - Sealed classes, to which adding members is compatible. Interfaces would make additions an S7 break.
- [x] CHK013 - Are the set-once state transitions and their failure codes specified? [Completeness, Data model §State of a set-once slot]
- [x] CHK014 - Is the format of the configuration revision marker specified, together with its owning spec? [Clarity, Data model `ConfigurationRevision`]
  - 1 to 64 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `-`. ISK-0057 decides what it names.

## Version Tags and Ownership

- [x] CHK015 - Is the version tag on types and later members specified, including how it relates to the package's contract ID? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027, Contract rules V1, V3]
- [x] CHK016 - Is every contract section assigned a review owner? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Contract header]
- [x] CHK017 - Is the way later specs change this contract (codes, types, wire versions, categories) specified? [Completeness, Contract §Changing this contract, Spec §FR-026]

## Boundaries and Scope

- [x] CHK018 - Is it clear that HTTP, OpenAI, and stream-event mappings belong to other specs, and which ones? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026, Out of Scope]
- [x] CHK019 - Are the exclusions (provider mapping, storage, ingress, packages) stated in measurable form? [Measurability, Spec §FR-044, SC-009]
- [x] CHK020 - Are AV-1 to AV-5 each assigned to the spec that validates them? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions needing validation]
- [x] CHK021 - Is the documentation-gate route (README and CONTRIBUTING links, no `docs/` topic change) consistent with FR-043? [Consistency, Spec §FR-043, Research R14]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
